title: The Man Who Discovered Whitney Houston and Bruce Springsteen Has Died at 94
summary: Have you ever heard a song that gave you goosebumps? Clive Davis spent his life finding songs—and singers—that made millions of people feel exactly that. The famous record executive, who helped launch the careers of Whitney Houston, Bruce Springsteen, Aretha Franklin, and many more, died at age 94. His family confirmed the news on social media, calling him "the iconic music legend whose vision shaped the soundtrack of countless lives." Davis didn't start in music. He was a lawyer who moved to Columbia Records at age 28. He quickly learned how the music business worked and became president of the company. He had a special talent: he could listen to a new artist and just feel they would be a star. He called it trusting his "instinct, this natural flow of energy." Later, he started his own label, Arista, and signed Whitney Houston when she was only 19. She went on to have seven number-one hits in a row! Davis also helped hip-hop and R&B grow through artists like Usher and Outkast. Even in his 90s, he hosted a star-studded pre-Grammys party every year. He once said, "There is no greater thrill than when you discover a terrific song. You can feel it down into your spine." Clive Davis truly felt the music—and helped us feel it too.
why_it_matters: This story reminds us that the people behind the scenes—the ones who believe in artists—can change how we feel through music, and maybe one day you could discover something amazing too.

background_read: Clive Davis was one of the most powerful people in the music industry. He worked at major record labels like Columbia Records and later founded Arista Records. He had a gift for spotting talent; he discovered Whitney Houston (a singer who had seven number-one songs in a row), Bruce Springsteen (a rock legend known as 'The Boss'), and Aretha Franklin (the Queen of Soul).

The Grammys are the biggest music awards in the United States, and Davis's annual pre-Grammy party became a famous event where stars gathered. Davis helped bring hip-hop and R&B music into the mainstream, shaping what millions of people listen to today.
Article_Structure: WHO: Clive Davis, a famous record executive who discovered Whitney Houston, Bruce Springsteen, and Aretha Franklin.
WHAT: He passed away at 94, leaving behind a legacy of hit songs and music legends.
WHERE: His family announced the news on social media, and tributes poured in from around the world.
WHY: Because his talent for finding great music gave people joy and shaped the soundtrack of their lives.

perspectives.description: Music fans celebrate the incredible artists Davis brought to the world; his 'ear' for a hit song made him a legend who gave millions goosebumps.
Some might say the music industry can be tough on young artists, and not every discovery story is as happy as Whitney Houston's; fame can come with great pressure.
Davis's legacy shows how one person's instinct and determination can influence an entire culture for decades, shaping not just music but how people experience it.
